translation_notes: LE cas de la strate : `if self.graph.value(pp, RDF.first):` -> `if bool(m{ {pp} rdf:first ?x }):` -- teste si un blank node est la tete d'une rdf:List. Demontre vrai (chemins sequence ecrits `( ... )`, cas1/cas7 de fixture.ttl) et faux/zero-solution (blank nodes sh:inversePath / sh:zeroOrMorePath a predicat unique, cas3/cas4, qui portent des predicats sans jamais avoir rdf:first -- voisinage direct du cas vrai).
`self.graph.value(current, RDF.first)` / `RDF.rest` (dans la boucle sequence) -> `m{ {current} rdf:first ?f }.first()` / `m{ {current} rdf:rest ?r }.first()`.

`list(self.graph.predicate_objects(subject=pp))` -> `list(m{ {pp} ?p ?o })` : arite 2, les lignes se destructurent directement en `bn_pred, bn_obj = pred_objects[0]`, sans devoir nommer un troisieme terme fixe.

`self.graph` est designe une fois (`@graph self.graph`, un attribut, pas un simple nom -- confirme : accepte tel quel) et couvre les quatre `m{ }` de la fonction ; aucun n'a besoin de nommer le graphe.

`Collection(self.graph, bn_obj)` (les deux occurrences, sh:union et sh:alternativePath) reste du rdflib brut : ce n'est pas un motif de triplet mais un algorithme (materialiser une rdf:List entiere), meme statut que .cbd() -- hors de portee de m{ } par construction, pas un manque du langage.

les classes reelles (PropertyPath et ses sous-classes) sont des pydantic BaseModel ; pydantic n'est pas installe dans cet environnement, donc le shim les reproduit en dataclasses de meme forme -- l'egalite structurelle par defaut des dataclasses est exactement l'oracle qu'il fallait, sans harnais de comparaison ad hoc.

harnais demo() (identique des deux cotes, meme convention que l'exemple `remove`) : recherche le noeud de chemin ancre a `ex:{anchor} ex:path`, appelle la region contre un PropertyShapeStub frais, et renvoie (resultat, appels a _add_path_to_shape) -- le stub relie sa propre recursion (`self._parse_property_path`) a l'implementation sous test via les globals de l'appelant, pour que la recursion du sh:sequence/inversePath reste a l'interieur de la version comparee.

REPAIR 2026-10-27: the guard `if self.graph.value(pp, RDF.first):` tests the TRUTH of the head element, not the existence of an rdf:first: `bool(m{ {pp} rdf:first ?x })` sent a list headed by "" or 0 into the list branch (ValueError "Malformed RDF list structure") where the original falls through to predicate_objects (ValueError "multiple predicate-objects"). Proved by the strengthened driver (err7/err8, FAIL with `bool`). Translation is now `if m{ {pp} rdf:first ?x }.first():`, the same truthiness as `value(...)`.

repair.driver: fixture + 6 valid cases (sh:oneOrMorePath, sh:zeroOrOnePath, shext:bNodeDepth, 3-level nesting, empty sh:alternativePath, empty sh:union) and 9 error cases (no predicate-object, several, unsupported construct, literal node, malformed list: falsy element / missing rdf:rest, falsy list head "" and 0, error from the recursion); driver.py compares the 9 exceptions (type + message, bnode ids normalised) of both artefacts, which run_pair cannot do on messages that embed blank-node ids; docstring explains each.
repair.remaining: The raise "Unhandled path class" is dead code in the source (every key of PRED_TO_PATH_CLASS is handled before or in the list of four) and is not exercised. Collection() stays rdflib (algorithm, not a pattern). Classification and article status for Maxime.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: the if/elif/else nesting is flattened into guard clauses: `if not isinstance(pp, BNode): raise ...` right after the URIRef case, `if not first: raise` before the append, `if len(pred_objects) > 1: raise` before the unpacking, and the PRED_TO_PATH_CLASS branch becomes `path_class = PRED_TO_PATH_CLASS.get(bn_pred)` followed by the two returns and the two raises (Unsupported when `path_class is None`, then the dead Unhandled raise, kept). `union_list` and `inner_path` are inlined, `predicate_objects(subject=pp)` loses its keyword, and the raise messages are no longer wrapped. Every raise survives with its message.

Kept on purpose: `list(Collection(...))` in the sh:union loop and in `alt_list`. A lazy iteration would call `_add_path_to_shape` or parse members before a recursive rdf:rest raises its ValueError, which changes what happens on an input the driver does not use.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `@graph self.graph` once, the three `self.graph.value(...)` become `m{ {node} rdf:first ?x }.first()` / `rdf:rest` (the guard keeps value()'s truth test, as the translation's repair requires), `predicate_objects` becomes `list(m{ {pp} ?p ?o })`, and RDF.nil, SH.union, SH.alternativePath become prefixed names. Measured: keeping Python's `.value()` and only islanding predicate_objects is 2 tokens longer, so the islands stay.
No exception to the symmetry rule. Collection() stays rdflib on both sides (an algorithm over an rdf:List, not a pattern).
header_optimization_notes: Python: RDFS, Graph, XSD and Literal go; RDF, SH and Node are imported from rdflib with BNode, Namespace and URIRef (one import instead of three).
LD Python: RDFS, Graph, XSD, Literal, RDF and SH go (RDF and SH are only written as prefixed names); Node joins the rdflib import; the rdfs: and xsd: @prefix lines go, rdf: and sh: stay.
